newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINLAND SAYS 1999 BUDGET SPENDING, DEFICIT TO FALL.
newsitem.headline: FINLAND SAYS 1999 BUDGET SPENDING, DEFICIT TO FALL.

text.p: Finnish Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto said on Wednesday the government had agreed the trend in state budget spending and the deficit was falling.
Niinisto said they would fall in 1998 compared to this year and drop again in 1999 versus 1998.
"This principle has been generally accepted," Niinisto told a news conference on the first day of the five-party coalition's talks on the 1998 state budget proposal.

Niinisto said the government had agreed on 188 billion markka ($33.7 billion) in total 1998 budget spending and on a deficit of about 17 to 18 billion markka, down from around 192 billion and 25 billion, respectively, this year.
The 1998 budget deficit would be roughly the same as the state's net borrowing requirement, he said.
State finances include expenditure items outside the budget, and the government may in some years request parliament's authorisation for more net borrowing than the budget deficit.

In the 1998 budget, expenditure threatened to increase by about 950 million markka due to the stronger U.S. dollar, Niinisto said. The government would be forced to find an equally big amount of new savings, he said.
Budget talks are scheduled to be completed on Friday.
The government's 1998 state budget proposal will be given to parliament on September 2.
